name: Take Us To Your Leader Postcard

config.theme: Advocate campaign postcard, retro flying-saucer gag. A little spaceship has landed and opened in a warm office; the 'aliens' who step out are recognizably a LEAGUE KID and a friendly HUMANOID ROBOT. They greet a bemused adult and ask to be taken to the leader. Second read: the 'aliens' are your kid and the robot they built — and they want to meet your boss. The ask is one warm introduction.
config.scene_description: On the landscaped central lawn of a sleek modern corporate research campus (glass-and-concrete engineering building simplified in the background, grassy plaza, sidewalks, a few trees and flowers, with the word \"TechnoCorp\" mounted on the building in the same clean bold sans-serif signage lettering style previously used for QUALCOMM), a classic 1950s flying saucer has just landed with its ramp lowered. A confident young inventor (about 13) has stepped out beside a friendly humanoid robot companion; the child stands with one hand extended toward a passing engineer, the robot politely attentive just behind. The engineer, carrying a briefcase and notebook on his way into work, has stopped on the sidewalk — surprised and amused, not frightened.

A sleek finished disc with no visible wires or circuit boards. Scary, dark, menacing, or invasion mood. Death rays, weapons, explosions, city destruction. Children (the human is a friendly adult 'leader'). More than one robot or more than one adult. Photorealism, 3D render, CGI, photographic faces. Portrait/vertical orientation. A black or dark box behind the League logo. Invented signs, labels, or lettering beyond the exact text specified. The word QUALCOMM or any other real company name/trademark on the building. Misspelled TechnoCorp. Blurry or muddy.
config.custom_additions:

The finished robot must read as 'the thing a kid built in class, now flying' — a home-made saucer, obviously hand-assembled, NOT a sleek chrome Hollywood UFO and NOT a metal alien.

TOP MASTHEAD BAND (about the top 22% of the card): a flat deep navy band spanning the full width, carrying the League wordmark "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" in the SAME 1950s pulp comic display lettering as the front of this postcard: "THE LEAGUE OF" smaller in cream, "AMAZING" largest and boldest in League orange, "PROGRAMMERS" medium in cream — all bold condensed caps with heavy black keylines, a confident hand-drawn pulp-comic feel. A small flat orange lightning bolt flanks each end of the top line. Energetic, crisp ink linework matching the front's style exactly.

2. OPEN ZONE (the remaining ~78% of the card): ONE single, completely FLAT, EMPTY cream field spanning the full width down to the bottom edge — no texture, no gradient, no illustration, no decorative elements, and ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT of any kind. This area is intentionally left blank; advocate-campaign message text will be added separately afterward.

A thin flat ink-black rule separates the navy masthead band from the cream field below it.

TEXT — the ONLY lettering anywhere on this card is the masthead wordmark "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS", spelled exactly as given, in its three-line stacked form. No other words, no placeholder text, no lorem ipsum, no addresses, no stamps box, no postal markings, nothing else anywhere on the card.

FORMAT — 4×6 inch landscape postcard back, full-bleed, print-ready quality.
iterations.negative_prompt: Any characters, people, robots, saucers, vehicles, or illustrated scene of any kind. Any text, lettering, numbers, or symbols in the cream field below the masthead — it must be completely empty and flat. Placeholder text, lorem ipsum, "your message here", sample address lines, a postage stamp box, postal cancellation marks, a QR code, barcodes. Texture, grain, gradient, noise, speckle, halftone, Ben-Day dots, newsprint, parchment, aged paper. Painted or airbrushed shading, soft glows, glossy highlights, 3D render, CGI, photorealism. A single-line masthead instead of the three-line stacked wordmark. Misspelled or reworded masthead text. Anime or manga style, chibi proportions, Funko-Pop style. Portrait orientation. Any element from the front-of-card scene (saucer, robot, kid, engineer, TechnoCorp building, TAKE US TO YOUR LEADER title) appearing on this back template.
iterations.custom_additions:
STYLE: bold retro 1950s PULP SCI-FI COMIC-BOOK cover art — heavy confident black ink outlines, hard-edged cel shading, punchy high-contrast flat comic color, light and playful (this is a friendly gag, not a scary invasion).

ROBOT BUILD — CRITICAL: use the reference photo ONLY for the ROBOT'S physical construction — the maker-built metal-beam kit chassis with bolt-holes, tangled red/yellow/blue wires, small circuit boards, and the ultrasonic-sensor two-round-eye 'face'. Do NOT copy the reference's composition. The finished robot must read as 'the thing a kid built in class, now flying' — a home-made saucer, obviously hand-assembled, NOT a sleek chrome Hollywood UFO and NOT a metal alien.

TEXT (render ONLY this, spelled EXACTLY, crisp — no other lettering anywhere):
- TITLE masthead across the TOP: "TAKE US TO YOUR LEADER" in huge bold retro pulp comic letters (red with heavy black outline) on a jagged burst — 1950s sci-fi movie-poster lettering.
- League logo in the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, sitting directly on the art with NO black or dark box behind it: "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" stacked wordmark, orange "AMAZING", small lightning bolts, bar-lines over "OF".

Deep navy comic border frame (solid flat navy). Exactly ONE robot-saucer and ONE friendly adult. Keep it warm, friendly, and funny.
